samples.summary: The strengthened font-readiness gate can pass vacuously: `fonts.check()` returns true when no matching FontFace is registered yet, and the new catch-all poll is trivially true for an empty/unregistered font set
samples.evidence: waitForFontsReady() now polls `document.fonts.check(`${weight} 12px "${family}"`)` for newly added families (Inter, Fraunces, JetBrains Mono) plus new weights 500/600. Per the CSS Font Loading spec, check() returns false only when a *matching* face is in `loading` status; when the Google Fonts stylesheet has not yet registered any face for the family (exactly the race the change claims to close), there are no matching faces and check() returns true immediately. The follow-up poll `[...document.fonts].every(face => face.status !== 'loading')` (line 394) is likewise satisfied by an empty or fully-'unloaded' font set. So the gate the change adds can be green while the very Inter face that caused the drift is unusable — the assertion holds whether or not the fixed behavior works.

samples.summary: `document.fonts.load(...).catch(() => {})` swallows load failures, and the in-code comment's claim that the check pass will report them as a named timeout is not true
samples.evidence: The comment at lines 371-373 asserts 'a rejection here means the fetch failed, which the check pass below reports as a timeout naming the family'. The check pass (line 384-393) calls fonts.check(), which returns true when no matching face is registered, so a family whose CSS never loaded produces neither a rejection (swallowed) nor a timeout. Previously an unresolvable load() rejected and failed page.evaluate(), i.e. the harness could fail; after this change that failure mode is silently absorbed, weakening the only signal the harness had.

samples.summary: The visual-harness font-wait rewrite (new families, new weights, reordered wait after section mount, new catch-all poll) ships with no test or self-check of any kind
samples.evidence: Grepped the repo for `waitForFontsReady`/`verify-visual-browser`: the only non-doc hits are the script itself, packages/frontend/package.json and scripts/run-browser-tests-docker.sh — no vitest/node:test file exercises it, and packages/frontend/scripts has no test directory. The change's only validation is that the browser visual lane happens to stay green, which (per the vacuity concerns above) it can do even if the gate never actually waits for a font. At minimum the reorder-after-mount claim ('Chromium only requests a face once text using it is laid out') is asserted purely in a comment.

samples.summary: files download: the `res.ok && !res.bytes` branch that also routes through upstreamErrorJson is not exercised
samples.evidence: runFilesDownload guards `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes)` (packages/cli/src/files/download.ts:56). The new test only feeds `{ok:false,...}` bodies, so the ok-but-empty-body case — where `res.data` is typically the success payload rather than an error envelope, and upstreamErrorJson would now emit HTTP_ERROR with a 2xx status string — is untested.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists verbatim (verify-visual-browser.mjs:384-398), but it is not a test assertion — it is a pre-screenshot stabilization wait. The harness's actual assertion is the pixel comparison against committed baselines (compareImages :193-235; comparison loop :552-599; hard exit at :623-628; baselines such as harness-visual.browser.slides-theme-panel.desktop.dark.png are committed and, per the task doc :5-18, encode Inter glyphs). Therefore a too-permissive font gate can only produce a FALSE FAILURE (the fallback-serif render is exactly what failed in PR #770), never a green run with unusable Inter: the claim "the assertion holds whether or not the fixed behavior works" is contradicted by the comparison code. Additionally, the reviewer's vacuity premise ("no face registered for the family") does not hold for the three families the change adds: index.html:8-12 statically requests Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono in <head>, and capturePass navigates with waitUntil "networkidle" (:416) and waits for root (:423) and section-ready (:426-429) before calling waitForFontsReady (:434), so matching @font-face rules are registered before check() is polled. Baseline rewriting requires an explicit UPDATE_VISUAL_BROWSER_BASELINE opt-in (:15, :524-547), so no fake baseline is produced by a verification run. Real-or-not, this is harness wait-logic strictness (correctness/flake lens), not vacuous coverage, missing tests, or over-mocking under the test-adequacy rubric.
